components.name: Indoor Case
components.description:
Build an indoor ventilation case (room + inlets + outlets + sinks + sources) for OpenFOAM 12. Isothermal by default. Wiring a Wall Temp, an Indoor Wall with a temperature or heat load, or a Heat Source switches it to the buoyant solver (foamRun -solver fluid: gravity, an energy equation and a temperature-dependent density), so temperature differences drive the flow — plumes, downdraughts, stratification, stack effect. The solve is steady unless Transient gives the buoyant solver a duration to integrate over. Method: De Simone, Kastner & Dogan (2021), Building Simulation 2021, Bruges, doi:10.26868/25222708.2021.30632.

Version 1.15.0.827

inputs.name: Case Name
inputs.description: Case name (no spaces). Leave empty for an auto-generated name (same convention as Outdoor).

inputs.name: Working Directory
inputs.description: Working directory (default ~/Eddy3D/Indoor).

inputs.name: Room
inputs.description: Closed room Brep.

inputs.name: Cell Size
inputs.description: Mesh cell size (m).

inputs.name: Inlets
inputs.description: Inlet surface(s): Brep or Indoor Inlet component(s).

inputs.name: Outlets
inputs.description: Outlet surface(s): Brep or Indoor Outlet component(s).

inputs.name: Inlet Speed
inputs.description: Fallback inlet speed (m/s) when raw Breps are used. Ignored when Indoor Inlet components provide velocity.

inputs.name: Sinks
inputs.description: Momentum sinks (Indoor Sink).

inputs.name: Sources
inputs.description: Emitters: Momentum / Heat / CO2 / Viral Source components.

inputs.name: Wall Temp
inputs.description: Optional wall temperature (K) for every room face no Indoor Wall covers. Setting it switches the case to the buoyant solver on its own; no Heat Source is needed.

inputs.name: Walls
inputs.description: Optional Indoor Wall components with a Surface: each gets its own patch and temperature. Room faces not covered by one keep the case-wide Wall Temp.

inputs.name: Age of Air
inputs.description: Solve the mean age of air (OpenFOAM 'age' function object) during the run. Age [s] is the time since the air at each point entered the room — the ventilation map: low = well flushed, high = trapped in a corner the supply never reaches. Unlike an air-change rate, which is one number for the whole room, it says WHERE the ventilation fails. Adds a cheap scalar transport solved at each write; probe the 'age' field to read it. Optional; default is off.

inputs.name: Transient
inputs.description: Optional simulated time in SECONDS. Leave empty for the steady solve, which answers where a room settles. Set it to follow how the room gets there — a warm-up, a cool-down, a plume that never settles: the buoyant solver then integrates in time under a Courant limit and keeps 20 snapshots over the run. Buoyant cases only (it needs a Wall Temp, an Indoor Wall with a temperature or heat load, or a Heat Source), and far more expensive than the steady solve.

inputs.name: Extras
inputs.description: Optional user additions from the Refinement Region and Custom Function Object components. Applied every time the case is written, so they survive a re-write. The indoor mesh dict is built programmatically and has no refinementRegions block of its own — one is created for a user region.

inputs.name: Location In Mesh
inputs.description: Optional point inside the room's AIR (snappyHexMesh's locationInMesh): the mesh keeps only the region connected to it. Leave empty to have one chosen — the room centre when that is open air, otherwise the point of the main air volume furthest from every surface. Set it when the room has several disconnected air volumes and the one to mesh is not the largest.

inputs.name: Engine
inputs.description: OpenFOAM execution environment for this case: BlueCFD, WSL, or Containerized (Docker/Podman). Read by the Run component.

inputs.name: Write
inputs.description: Click to write the case to disk. Resets automatically so it never re-writes on recompute.

inputs.name: Clear
inputs.description: Click to delete the case folder. Resets automatically so it never re-deletes on recompute.

outputs.name: Case
outputs.description: The indoor case (for the Run component).

outputs.name: Logs
outputs.description: Build / write logs.

components.name: Wind Rose Cluster
components.description:
Cluster annual wind conditions into a budget of representative directions using k-means over hourly wind vectors (speed x direction): frequent, strong conditions attract the budget, and each cluster reports an observed direction/speed pair plus its frequency. Without wired speeds, clusters directions alone (unit vectors). Method: Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639; Kastner & Dogan (2019), Building Simulation 2019, Rome 621-628, doi:10.26868/25222708.2019.210458.

Version 1.15.0.827

inputs.name: Directions
inputs.description: Wind directions in degrees (e.g. hourly values from an EPW).

inputs.name: Budget
inputs.description: Maximum number of representative directions (clusters), e.g. 8 or 16.

inputs.name: Wind Speeds
inputs.description: Hourly wind speeds (m/s) paired with Directions (optional). When wired, the clustering runs over wind VECTORS (speed x direction), so speed and frequency both shape the representative set; calm hours (< 0.5 m/s) are excluded.

outputs.name: Wind Directions
outputs.description: Distinct representative wind directions in degrees, sorted ascending; plug into the ABL or Uniform Flow component's Wind Directions input.

outputs.name: Wind Speeds
outputs.description: Representative wind speed (m/s) per cluster — the observed speed of the cluster's medoid hour, aligned with Wind Directions; plug into the ABL component's Wind Speed input. Requires wired input speeds.

outputs.name: Frequencies
outputs.description: Fraction of (non-calm) hours in each cluster, aligned with Wind Directions — the per-direction weights for annual wind-comfort statistics. Sums to 1.

Build a lattice-Boltzmann wind case from the ABL, the geometry and a settings object, and write it to disk. Wire 'LBM Run Settings' for OpenLB or 'FluidX3D Run Settings' for FluidX3D (nothing = OpenLB). Feed the Case output to LBM Run, then to Probe, LBM Field or FluidX3D Live View — the same Case → Run → Probe chain as the OpenFOAM wind study.

The auto extents follow COST 732/Franke best practice (5H inflow, 15H wake, 5H sides/top); the case component verifies the resulting blockage against ASCE/SEI CWE Prestandard AC 6-8b. Model surrounding buildings within ~240 m of the study area (ASCE 49 proximity guidance) before trusting results near the context edge.

inputs.name: Cell Size
inputs.description: Base cell size for the domain in meters. Default: 20.

inputs.name: Front Extension
inputs.description: Upwind padding in front of the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 5x the building height.

inputs.name: Back Extension
inputs.description: Downwind padding behind the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 15x the building height.

inputs.name: Side Extension
inputs.description: Padding on the side faces of the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 5x the building height.

inputs.name: Top Extension
inputs.description: Padding above the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 5x the building height.

inputs.name: Refinement Box Extension
inputs.description: Padding of the refinement box around the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 27.5% of the building footprint.

inputs.name: Wake Refinement
inputs.description: How far the refinement box extends downwind into the building's wake, as a multiple of the base padding (1 = symmetric, 3 = best-practice default). Upwind/lateral stay at the base.

outputs.name: Domain Parameters
outputs.description: Domain and refinement box parameters (-1 entries mean auto-sized from the building geometry); plug into the wind case Domain input. The resolved domain is the wind case component's Domain output.

components.name: Cylinder Domain
components.description: Define a cylindrical simulation domain for Eddy3D. One cylindrical mesh serves all wind directions; the cylinder side faces switch between inlet and outlet per direction. The auto radius targets the 3% frontal-blockage limit of ASCE/SEI CWE Prestandard AC 6-8b, which the case component verifies. Model surrounding buildings within ~240 m of the study area (ASCE 49 proximity guidance) before trusting results near the context edge. Method: Kastner & Dogan (2020), Journal of Building Performance Simulation 13(1):59-68, doi:10.1080/19401493.2019.1692906; Kastner & Dogan (2018), eSim 2018 (IBPSA-Canada), Montréal, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325023244_Streamlining_meshing_methodologies_for_annual_urban_CFD_simulations.

inputs.name: Core Cell Size
inputs.description: Cell size of the inner core blocks in meters. Default: 25.

inputs.name: Inner Core Size
inputs.description: Half-size of the square inner core in meters. -1 = auto from the building footprint.

inputs.name: Outer Radius
inputs.description: Outer radius of the cylindrical domain in meters. -1 = auto from the building height.

inputs.name: Height
inputs.description: Height of the cylindrical domain in meters. -1 = auto from the building height.

inputs.name: Radial Multiplier
inputs.description: Cell growth factor from the core toward the perimeter. Default: 2.

inputs.name: Core Divisions
inputs.description: Cells per core block (and per perimeter segment, tangentially). Refines the core without changing the block layout that Core Cell Size sets; the preview core grid densifies to match. Default: 1.

inputs.name: Refinement Box Extension
inputs.description: Padding of the refinement box around the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 27.5% of the building footprint.

inputs.name: Radial Grading
inputs.description: Far-field cell coarsening across the perimeter ring (outer cell size / inner cell size). 1 = uniform; >1 keeps fine cells at the buildings but grows the outer cells. The default 7 coarsens the far field aggressively (far fewer cells downwind); lower it (1-3) for a gentler, more uniform ring. Default: 7.

inputs.name: Core Roundness
inputs.description: Rounds the O-grid inner core from a square (0) toward a circle (1). Higher values even out the radial gap to the outer boundary, cutting the corner non-orthogonality of the square core. 0 keeps the classic square core. 0.65 is the checkMesh-sweep optimum (lowest max non-orthogonality across mesh resolutions; skewness stays well within limits). Default: 0.65.

inputs.name: Vertical Grading
inputs.description: Vertical cell expansion ratio (top cell size / bottom cell size). 1 = uniform; >1 keeps fine cells near the ground and coarsens aloft (typical for an ABL). A checkMesh sweep showed non-orthogonality/skewness are unaffected by this; the only cost is background aspect ratio. The default 35 strongly refines the near-ground layer; ease it down if convergence struggles. Default: 35.

outputs.name: Domain Parameters
outputs.description: Cylindrical domain parameters (-1 entries mean auto-sized from the building geometry); plug into the wind case Domain input.

components.name: Pedestrian Wind Comfort

Classifies pedestrian wind comfort per point from an annual hourly wind-speed series (the Wind Speed output of the Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) component) against a comfort criterion (Lawson, Davenport, NEN8100). Returns the comfort category, class letter, and activity description for each point.

Version 1.15.0.827

inputs.name: Wind Speed
inputs.description: Annual wind field from the Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) component (its Wind Speed output): a single object holding every point's 8760-hour wind-speed series. Passed as an object so the millions of values skip the Grasshopper data tree.

inputs.name: Comfort Metric
inputs.description: Comfort criterion: Lawson General, Lawson LDDC, Lawson 2001, Davenport, NEN8100 Comfort, NEN8100 Safety, or Wellington (NZ; its safety class reads the 3-second gust). A wired integer 0-6 (the old convention) still selects by index. A Criteria object wired below overrides this pick.

inputs.name: Color Scheme
inputs.description: Categorical palette for the comfort classes: Classic (green through red, the standard wind-comfort plot), Colorblind Safe (Okabe-Ito derived), or Muted (desaturated, for underlays).

inputs.name: Size
inputs.description: Marker half-size in model units for the comfort mesh (one quad per point).

inputs.name: Period
inputs.description: Slice of the year to classify: Year (default), a season, or a single month. The exceedance criteria then apply to that period's hours only — winter comfort is usually worse than annual. Seasons are named by their months (Winter = Dec-Feb), so southern-hemisphere EPWs read unambiguously.

inputs.name: Gust Speed
inputs.description: Optional annual gust field — the Gust Speed output of Velocity Amplification Factors (needs its TKE input). Read by gust-referenced classes only (Wellington's 20 m/s annual maximum 3-second gust). Without it those classes fall back to mean × Gust Factor.

Ignored when Gust Speed is wired.

inputs.name: Criteria
inputs.description: Optional criteria object from the Wind Comfort Criteria component — a jurisdiction's own class table. When wired it replaces the Comfort Metric pick.

outputs.name: Comfort Rank
outputs.description: Comfort category number per point (1 = most comfortable; higher = worse).

outputs.name: Class Letter
outputs.description: Comfort class letter per point (A, B, ... ; S = unsafe).

outputs.name: Comfort Class
outputs.description: Comfort activity description per point (e.g. Sitting, Walking).

outputs.name: Mesh

outputs.name: Colors
outputs.description: Class color per point, aligned with the input series — for coloring custom geometry.

outputs.name: Legend Colors
outputs.description: One color per class of the selected metric, best-to-worst — pairs with Legend Labels for annotation.

Optionally transfers the station's speeds to the site's terrain per EN 1991-1-4 (the anemometer stands in open country; the site does not).
